summary: Specifies DCCP-UDP, an alternative encapsulation of the Datagram Congestion Control Protocol that lets DCCP pass through current NAT middleboxes without modifying them. It also updates an earlier specification. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: Some doors only let one kind of package through. DCCP-UDP wraps DCCP packages inside the kind that is allowed, so they can get past.

subtitle: Wrapping DCCP in UDP so it can cross the NAT boxes that only understand UDP.

tldr.problem: Many deployed NAT and NAPT devices support UDP but not DCCP, so native DCCP packets cannot get through them.
tldr.mechanism: DCCP-UDP inserts a UDP header between the IP header and the DCCP packet, uses the UDP checksum in place of the DCCP checksum, and uses UDP port 6511 as the default listening port. SDP gets a new dccp-port attribute and new protocol identifiers to signal the encapsulation.
tldr.outcome: DCCP can traverse existing UDP-aware NATs without changing them, at the cost of extra header overhead and limited partial-checksum functionality.

today: RFC 6773 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 4340 and RFC 5762. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The NAT Problem for DCCP
sections.content:
The Datagram Congestion Control Protocol (DCCP) gives applications unreliable but congestion-controlled flows, and it normally rides directly in IPv4 or IPv6 packets. NAT behaviour for DCCP is specified in RFC 5597, but there is a large installed base of NAT and NAPT devices that follow RFC 4787 for UDP and do not support RFC 5597.

DCCP-UDP is an alternative encapsulation that works with that installed base. The ordinary encapsulation is called DCCP-STD. DCCP-UDP supports all DCCP-STD features, with limited functionality for partial checksums.

It may also serve as a transition mechanism for devices that support UDP but not yet DCCP, and it lets DCCP be implemented inside an application. The RFC warns that the extra UDP header can complicate inspection of DCCP fields by routers doing ECMP, load-sharing devices, firewalls and media gateways.
sections.eli5: Many home routers only know how to pass one kind of package. This memo wraps the other kind in that package so it can get through.

sections.title: The Basic Approach
sections.content:
A UDP header is inserted between the IP header and the DCCP packet. The RFC stresses that this is not tunnelling: the real IP addresses of the end systems stay in the IP header, and no extra addresses are embedded.

This suits NAT because a NAT rewrites addresses, which changes the transport checksum, and a NAPT may also rewrite ports, usually the source port. Both would be done on the outer UDP header, which the NAT already knows how to handle.

A DCCP-UDP server listens on a UDP port, by default 6511, or on a port agreed through out-of-band signalling such as SDP. It strips the UDP header and hands the packet to the DCCP module. One endpoint may offer DCCP-STD and DCCP-UDP, over IPv4 and IPv6, at the same time.
sections.eli5: It is like putting your letter in a second envelope with the kind of stamp the post office accepts. The address inside stays the same.

sections.title: The Headers on the Wire
sections.content:
A DCCP-UDP packet is the IP header, an 8-byte UDP header, the DCCP generic header (12 or 16 bytes), type-specific fields, DCCP options and the application data. The 12-byte form uses short 24-bit sequence numbers and the 16-byte form uses long 48-bit ones.

The UDP ports identify where the endpoints listen for DCCP-UDP packets. They do not identify the DCCP ports, which stay in the DCCP header. The UDP Length covers the UDP header and its payload. The UDP checksum is the Internet checksum over a network-layer pseudoheader and the UDP packet, and it MUST NOT be zero.
sections.eli5: There are two address labels now. The outer one is for the post office. The inner one says which person in the house the letter is for.

sections.title: Checksums, ECN, ICMP and Packet Size
sections.content:
The UDP checksum does the job of the DCCP checksum. This was chosen because existing NAT traversal methods for UDP do not know DCCP is inside and so would not fix an inner checksum. On sending, the DCCP Checksum field SHOULD be zero, and on receipt it MUST be ignored. A received packet MUST be dropped if the UDP checksum is zero or invalid, if the UDP Length is less than 20, or if the UDP Length does not fit the DCCP-UDP header and the packet.

DCCP partial checksums are still syntactically supported, as is negotiation of the Minimum Checksum Coverage feature, but the UDP checksum always covers the whole DCCP datagram. An application using partial checksums therefore gets a service functionally identical to full coverage.

An endpoint SHOULD follow the DCCP-STD ECN procedures from RFC 4340, and MUST follow its Path MTU Discovery rules. Encapsulation overhead reduces the DCCP Maximum Packet Size. ICMP errors relate to the UDP layer, and endpoints SHOULD forward them to the DCCP module. A minimal ICMP error only identifies the UDP ports, so an endpoint with several DCCP connections on one UDP port pair may not be able to tell which connection it concerns.
sections.eli5: The outer envelope gets the safety seal, and the inner seal is ignored. If the outer seal is missing or broken, the letter is thrown away.

sections.title: UDP Ports and Telling Connections Apart
sections.content:
Port 6511 is the default for a system-wide DCCP-UDP service, such as a daemon serving many DCCP applications. An application-specific implementation SHOULD instead use an ephemeral port, advertise it by other means such as SDP, and SHOULD NOT use the assigned port. Some NAT topologies need a non-default port.

A client SHOULD choose a distinct UDP source port for each DCCP connection. A server SHOULD accept datagrams from any UDP source port, and MUST identify an active connection by a 6-tuple: source and destination IP address, UDP port and DCCP port. This is because two hosts behind NAPTs could use the same DCCP source port.

Demultiplexing happens in two stages: first by the UDP 4-tuple, then by the 6-tuple. An implementation MUST implement exactly one of two methods.

  • Accept only one active 6-tuple per UDP 4-tuple. Other packets MUST NOT reach the DCCP module and the server SHOULD send a DCCP-Reset with Reset Code 12, "Encapsulated Port Reuse".
  • Support several DCCP connections over one UDP 4-tuple, mapping each 6-tuple to one connection and discarding packets it cannot match.
sections.eli5: The outer envelope only names the house. The inner one names the person, so the house needs a list of who is expecting mail.

sections.title: Signalling DCCP-UDP with SDP
sections.content:
Applications that signal DCCP parameters outside the protocol MUST define how the encapsulation is chosen and MUST allow either one to be signalled. If both are supported, DCCP-STD SHOULD be preferred. This section updates RFC 5762, which predates DCCP-UDP, so that SDP can describe RTP over it.

New protocol identifiers include UDP/DCCP, UDP/DCCP/RTP/AVP, UDP/DCCP/RTP/SAVP, UDP/DCCP/RTP/AVPF and UDP/DCCP/RTP/SAVPF. The port in the m= line is the UDP port of the encapsulation service. The DCCP port is carried in a new media-level attribute, a=dccp-port:, which MUST be included when these identifiers are used.

Using a=rtcp-mux is RECOMMENDED for RTP over DCCP-UDP, since without it the second demultiplexing method MUST be implemented or the RTCP connection will be rejected. Using ICE or SDP Capability Negotiation to pick between DCCP-UDP and native DCCP is left for future study.
sections.eli5: When two programs agree to talk, they also write down which envelope to use and which person inside the house gets the letter.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
DCCP-UDP has the same security measures and the same risks as DCCP-STD, and it keeps no extra state at the encapsulation layer. It exposes DCCP to the risks of passing through NATs but creates no new NAT risks. Endpoints should take precautions before acting on ICMP messages, as described for TCP in RFC 5927.

It may let DCCP through existing firewalls under UDP rules, if administrators choose, though full control of DCCP connections needs firewall enhancements. DTLS can protect individual DCCP connections, which leaves the UDP header unencrypted. It can also run over the encapsulating UDP transport, which protects the DCCP headers from middleboxes and avoids a separate handshake for each DCCP connection.
sections.eli5: Wrapping the letter does not make it safer or less safe by itself. If you want it private, you also need a locked box.

sections.title: IANA Allocations
sections.content:
IANA allocated UDP port 6511 for the DCCP-UDP service, allocated for a transport service rather than an application. It assigned DCCP Reset Code 12, "Encapsulated Port Reuse", which applies to all DCCP congestion control IDs. Its three data bytes carry the packet type that caused the error and the encapsulated UDP source port.

IANA also allocated the media-level SDP attribute dccp-port, with the long-form name "Encapsulated DCCP Port".
sections.eli5: The keeper of the list wrote down the mailbox number, the new error code and the new label for the forms.
